candidates.attacker_control: The XML document is read from the build workspace by analysis-core's `FilesParser` when a job has the CCM publisher/reporter enabled: `CcmPublisher.perform` passes the configured Ant pattern (default `**/*.cs` at CcmPublisher.java:60; the descriptor help/config.properties advertises `**/ccm.xml`) and `CcmReporter.perform` uses the fixed name `ccm.xml`. Workspace content is supplied by SCM checkout of the built repository, by build steps, or by Pipeline commands (the repo's own WorkflowCompatibilityTest copies a workspace file and invokes `step([$class: 'CcmPublisher'])`), so an attacker who can commit to a built repository or run/configure a job controls the bytes fed to Digester. The in-repo payload templates `testXxe-xxe.xml`/`testXxe-oob.xml` show the exact parameter-entity/OOB and target-URL variants expected against this parser.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Searched the whole snapshot for XXE mitigations (`setFeature`, `EntityResolver`, `HudsonDigesterFactory`, `SAXParser`, `XMLInputFactory`) - none exist; only `new Digester()` at CcmParser.java:87. Verified `setValidating(false)` does not disable DTD/entity expansion and that `setClassLoader` is unrelated. Confirmed the legitimate test reports (`ccm.result.xml`, `pynamodb_ccm_results_sample.xml`) contain no DOCTYPE, so disabling DTDs would not break normal parsing. Confirmed no other XML-parsing code path in the repo, and no global JAXP/secure-processing setup. Checked that `Metric`/`Ccm` setters used by Digester rules introduce no class-instantiation gadget, so the impact is the classic XXE triad rather than Digester rule RCE.
candidates.impact: XXE against the Jenkins process hosting the build workspace: (1) confidentiality - external `SYSTEM` entities can read local files usable in entity values (e.g. `file:///...`) and exfiltrate them out-of-band through parameter entities, as modeled by `testXxe-xxe.xml`; (2) SSRF - external entity/DTD URLs make the Jenkins JVM issue requests to arbitrary internal hosts/ports, as modeled by `testXxe-oob.xml`'s `$TARGET_URL$`; (3) availability - unbounded entity expansion (billion laughs) can exhaust memory/CPU in the Jenkins JVM. Values pulled into `Metric`/`Bug` fields are also rendered in Jenkins result views, which can provide an in-band disclosure channel.
candidates.prerequisites: The CCM publisher (freestyle/Pipeline) or Maven reporter must be configured for a job that runs, and an attacker-influenced workspace file must match the configured include pattern (freestyle default `**/*.cs`, Maven fixed `ccm.xml`, or the commonly configured `**/ccm.xml`). No Jenkins admin action is required beyond the job configuration itself; the parse happens in the JVM hosting the workspace (controller or agent) with that process's file and network access.
candidates.root_cause: `CcmParser.parseCCMXmlFile` creates a fresh `org.apache.commons.digester.Digester` and only calls `setValidating(false)` and `setClassLoader(...)` before `digester.parse(ccmXmlFile)` (CcmParser.java:86-107, call at 106). It never sets `http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl` (or external-general-entities/external-parameter-entities to false), never installs a denying EntityResolver, and never enables secure processing. `setValidating(false)` suppresses DTD validation but does not stop DTD processing or external entity resolution, so DOCTYPE declarations, parameter entities, and `SYSTEM` entities in the report file are processed by the underlying JAXP SAX parser. No hardening exists anywhere else in the plugin (searches for `setFeature`, `EntityResolver`, `HudsonDigesterFactory`, `SAXParser`, `XMLInputFactory` return no matches).
candidates.title: XXE in CcmParser: unhardened Apache Commons Digester parses untrusted workspace CCM XML reports
candidates.trace: `CcmPublisher.perform` (CcmPublisher.java:93-105) builds `new FilesParser(PLUGIN_NAME, pattern, new CcmParser(getDefaultEncoding()), ...)` and invokes `workspace.act(pmdCollector)`; analysis-core opens each matching workspace file and calls `AbstractAnnotationParser.parse(File, String)`, which the plugin overrides at `CcmParser.parse(InputStream, String)` (CcmParser.java:67-84). That method calls `parseCCMXmlFile(file)` (line 71), which constructs the unhardened `Digester` (lines 87-89) and calls `digester.parse(ccmXmlFile)` (line 106). Maven path: `CcmReporter.perform` (CcmReporter.java:130-136) → same `CcmParser`. The index confirms these call edges (`CcmPublisher.perform`/`CcmReporter.perform` → `CcmParser` ctor; `parse` → `parseCCMXmlFile`; `parseCCMXmlFile` → `new Digester()`), and source text confirms no entity/DTD restriction is applied.
candidates.unverified: The transitive `commons-digester` version is not declared in this POM (it comes from analysis-pom/analysis-core, and dependency JARs are not in the snapshot), so the exact default SAX features of the runtime classpath cannot be inspected here; however, Commons Digester does not disable DTDs/external entities by default and the plugin applies no explicit mitigation. Whether the parse runs on the controller or an agent, the JVM's file-read permissions, and whether a given deployment allows untrusted users to trigger a matching workspace file were not runtime-verified. No test or exploit was executed; exploitability is inferred from source and in-repo payload templates.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (XXE)

coverage_summary: Scope: 60 source-root files, 59 model-visible; 1 file was excluded by the sensitive-name/path filter, and no files were excluded for size or symlinks. The P1 relation index parsed 29 Java files (170 symbols, 310 call rows, 221 edges) and omitted 20 non-Java files (resources, XML fixtures, properties, HTML help, site.xml); control flow, data flow, and semantic resolution are not implemented, and Spring annotation facts are not applicable. I read all 29 Java files (main + tests) and all security-relevant non-Java files (pom.xml, config.properties, Messages.properties, the four test XML resources). Entry points `CcmPublisher.perform` and `CcmReporter.perform`, the parser, the Digester construction, and the model entities were verified against source text; the index was used only to confirm navigation (perform → CcmParser ctor, parse → parseCCMXmlFile → `new Digester()`). analysis-core/hudson/JAXP library internals (FilesParser, AbstractAnnotationParser, Digester, SAX parser defaults) are outside the snapshot and were not read; that external hop is the main gap in the call chain, supported only by the plugin's `@Override` contract and API usage.
limitations: Dependency JARs (commons-digester, analysis-core, Jenkins core) are absent from the snapshot, so the transitive Digester/SAX-parser version and its exact default entity-processing behavior could not be inspected; the finding relies on documented Commons Digester defaults plus the absence of any explicit hardening in the plugin source.

The hop from analysis-core's `FilesParser` to `AbstractAnnotationParser.parse(File, String)` and then to the overridden `CcmParser.parse(InputStream, String)` is inferred from the API usage and `@Override` annotation; the library source is not present to read directly.

No build, test, scanner, or exploit was executed, so exploitability is not runtime-confirmed; the relationship between job/workspace permissions and who can trigger parsing in a specific Jenkins deployment was not verified.

The relation index provides only syntactic call/containment candidates with no data/control flow, no semantic resolution, and 232 unresolved calls; non-Java files are not represented in the index, and one repository file was withheld by the sensitive-name filter.
Whether the parse executes on the Jenkins controller or a build agent (and thus which process's files/network are exposed) depends on the deployment and was not determined from source.

rejected_leads.lead: Potential NPE/DoS in CcmParser when a `<metric>` lacks `<classification>`: `metric.getClassification()` is dereferenced with `.contains(...)`/`.contentEquals(...)` in `isMetricHighPriority`/`isMetricModeratePriority` (CcmParser.java:154-178).
rejected_leads.reason: This is a robustness bug (NullPointerException on malformed input) with no confidentiality/integrity impact beyond a failed build; it is subsumed by the attacker's ability to supply malformed XML and is not a distinct security weakness.

rejected_leads.lead: CcmPublisher's `DEFAULT_PATTERN = "**/*.cs"` (CcmPublisher.java:60) conflicts with the UI help/config.properties that document `**/ccm.xml`, and text is parsed as XML from any matching `.cs` file.
rejected_leads.reason: Not a separate root cause; the pattern discrepancy only broadens which workspace files reach the same unhardened parser and is included as part of the XXE candidate's attacker-control analysis.
The interpolated values are integer counts and message counts from Messages.properties, not attacker-controlled strings; no injection is demonstrable from source.

rejected_leads.lead: `CcmResult` extends analysis-core `BuildResult`, which serializes annotations to `ccm-warnings.xml` (CcmResult.java:49,63-65).
rejected_leads.reason: The serialization implementation lives in the external analysis-core library, which is not in this snapshot; no unsafe deserialization or gadget chain is visible in the reviewed source, so this remains unconfirmed and was not pursued.
Dead/unreferenced test fixtures are not a vulnerability by themselves; they are used only as corroborating context for the parser finding, and no visible test consumes them.

summary: The repository is the Jenkins CCM plugin (3.2-SNAPSHOT). It parses build-workspace XML report files with Apache Commons Digester. In `CcmParser.parseCCMXmlFile` a `new Digester()` is configured with only `setValidating(false)` and `setClassLoader(...)`; no DTD/external-entity hardening is set and `digester.parse(ccmXmlFile)` is called directly on attacker-influenced input (CcmParser.java:86-107). The parser is reached from `CcmPublisher.perform` (freestyle/Pipeline, files selected by a workspace Ant pattern, default `**/*.cs`) and `CcmReporter.perform` (Maven, fixed `ccm.xml`), i.e. the XML content comes from the build workspace, which is normally controlled by the job/SCM/Pipeline content rather than by a trusted admin. The repository also contains unreferenced XXE payload templates (`testXxe-xxe.xml` with an OOB parameter entity and `testXxe-oob.xml` with a `$TARGET_URL$`), which corroborate the expected attack shape but are not themselves proof. The single strongest candidate is improper restriction of XML external entity references (CWE-611), enabling local file disclosure, SSRF/OOB exfiltration, and entity-expansion DoS against the Jenkins JVM that performs the parse. Everything else reviewed is thin glue code over analysis-core or is only a robustness issue; those are listed as rejected leads.
